data.narrative:
SiPearl is a Series A-stage semiconductor company that has raised €130M to date. The valuation exercise draws from a comparables universe of 11 private and public firms in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, comprising 8 private companies (including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent) and 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Standard peer-median methodology is not applicable here. The narrow peer set—filtered for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded only two datapoints, falling short of the three-company minimum required for reliable triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise given the wide dispersion in business models, capital intensity, and commercialization timelines across semiconductor subsectors. As a result, no quantitative valuation range can be supported by the available data.

Meaningful valuation synthesis requires either (1) expansion of the comparable set through additional Series A semiconductor companies, (2) application of alternative methods such as DCF or cost-of-capital approaches with forward assumptions, or (3) explicit reliance on recent transaction data for SiPearl's sector. The primary uncertainty is the absence of sufficient same-stage peers; until that constraint is resolved, any valuation conclusion would rest on incomplete triangulation.
